symptom: A Draft 2020-12 schema-only consumer admitted positive count-map entries whose synthetic keys embedded absolute POSIX, drive-letter, UNC or file-URL path tokens. The runtime validator already rejected these keys. Synthetic Python jsonschema and Node 22.16.0 probes established the cross-engine gap without reading any private paths, odds, databases or production evidence.
lesson: A JSON Schema propertyNames denylist for known private field names does not reject synthetic absolute filesystem path tokens hidden inside arbitrary diagnostic count-map keys. Schema-only validation must carry a lexical path guard independent of runtime validation, and Python/ECMAScript whitespace differences must be tested explicitly.
guardrail: Keep propertyNames.allOf with the existing exact private-key denylist and a second not.pattern for POSIX, drive-letter, UNC, file-URL and embedded path tokens. Use an explicit ECMAScript whitespace class rather than engine-specific \s; retain HTTPS and ordinary taxonomy negative controls, digest checks and runtime semantic validation. This is schema-only lexical hardening, not proof of data provenance or production authorization.
